A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same formula-unification research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison; the identified inconsistencies are in the documents themselves, not extraction gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original computational harvesting, validation, canonicalization, and formula-unification outcomes in Sections 2–3 and Appendices A and F.

after.justification: v2 reports original computational unification results and new empirical LLM comparisons, including extraction success rates and manually checked equivalence proofs in Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: Appendix B.3 extends the specified second-order solver to order-m recurrences, adding PSLQ-based construction of the initial transformation matrix from projective limits. Appendix B.1 replaces random hub selection with indexed matching and a global nonhubs list; B.2 reduces slow-convergence folding candidates from four to three. These are procedural changes beyond the UMAPS renaming.

E1.justification: The arXiv subject categories, cutoff date, and constants remain the same. However, v2 extends CMF-mapping evaluation to e and ζ(3), where v1 provided pairwise-equivalence examples, using explicit fields in Appendices A.2–A.3. The larger formula counts alone do not establish broader coverage.

E2.justification: v1 has no corresponding comparative evaluations. v2 compares GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview on equivalence detection and proving, and compares GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, and GPT-4o mini as extractors with a fixed GPT-4o mini classifier (Tables 2–3).

E3.justification: The reported CMF search changes from directions with maximum absolute coordinate below 10 and one starting point to coordinates at most 3 and 27 starting points (Appendix B.5). New protocols separately test detection and proving on ten formula pairs, manually check proofs, and pool validated extractions to establish reference data. The reported article count also changes from 457,145 to 455,050; this does not establish that every experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's individual extraction examples, v2 systematically tests sensitivity to extractor choice while holding the classifier fixed. Table 3 distinguishes executable-code failures from symbolic mistakes, providing substantial new evidence about a central pipeline component. Table 7 also identifies mathematical structures associated with individual LLM successes and failures.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new comparisons report counts and percentages without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v1 reports 95 of 254 analyzed second-order formulas in one CMF; v2 reports 188 of 407 validated formulas and relations among 381. Some retained formulas gain CMF connections, including v1 Table 7 row 32 becoming v2 Table 12 row 56. New LLM and e-unification results are added, and values are corrected, such as 2/π becoming −2/π between v1 Table 7 row 21 and v2 Table 13 row 128. Changed populations and search settings preclude interpreting aggregate increases as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds Lemma 2 and its higher-dimensional projective-limit proof in Appendix B.3.1, plus explicit e and ζ(3) CMFs. Appendix A.4 corrects the duplicated Sun recurrence from v1's proof exposition. Conversely, A.1.3 drops lower-degree terms from the retained U12 polynomial, making that displayed certificate fail the stated identity.

C1.justification: The central claim of automated formula unification and applicability beyond π remains. v2 adds a headline claim of relations among 94% of validated formulas and explicitly claims priority for symbolic unification at scale. These sharpen the contribution without replacing its central research objective.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of LLM performance, qualifies the unbounded convergence rates of the e examples, and explicitly excludes formal-language proof reconstruction from scope. Some detailed harvesting-improvement proposals from v1 Appendix E.7 disappear. The new claim that successful LLM relations require equal dynamical metrics conflicts with the unequal-rate folding example in Appendix C.3 and Table 7.

D1.justification: Building on v1's prompts and Colab access, v2 adds a project-repository link, CPU identification, an API-cost estimate below $50, benchmark prompts and pair identifiers, and more explicit CMF-generation instructions. The 200-term recurrence-fitting detail is retained elsewhere, while the earlier 4000-term limit-approximation instruction is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against automated theorem proving, conjecture generation, and AI discovery, adding works such as Trinh, Fajtlowicz, Fawzi, and Novikov alongside LLM translation research. It explicitly distinguishes symbolic unification as previously unaddressed. Many existing formula-source references are represented through arXiv identifiers rather than genuinely removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, mathematical background precedes a reorganized methodology, and benchmarking becomes a separate section. The solver receives the UMAPS name, Appendix A is reorganized around constants, and harvesting documentation is reordered. These changes substantially alter the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to predominantly single-column layout with wrapped figures. Figures 4–5 exchange positions, the CMF graph is updated, and new comparison, summary, and algorithm tables appear. Appendix result tables gain convergence-rate columns and expanded formula displays, while source mappings become a consolidated color-coded table.

improvement.justification: The controlled extractor comparison, expanded algorithm documentation, reproducibility disclosures, and corrected formula values make v2 more informative and assessable. These benefits are tempered by introduced defects: Appendix A.1.3 loses necessary certificate terms, and Section 4.1's equal-metric benchmark description conflicts with the successful unequal-rate example in Table 7. The evidence supports a limited net improvement rather than an unqualified substantial gain.
